{{Short description|Mathematician (born 1969)}}
'''Lei Ni''' (born 1969) is a mathematician. He holds [[emeritus professor]] status at the [[University of California, San Diego]] (UCSD). He was elected a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in 2018.

Ni was born in 1969,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ni, Lei, 1969-|url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n2006057655.html|website=LC Linked Data Service|access-date=2025-11-29|date=2025-08-05|publisher=[[Library of Congress]]}}</ref> and from 1987 to 1993 attended [[Fudan University]] in China, from where he received a B.S. and M.S. degree in mathematics. He studied at the [[University of California, Irvine]], from 1994 to 1998, and received a Ph.D. in mathematics,<ref name="home">{{Cite web|url=https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~lni/|title=Lei Ni's Home Page|access-date=2025-11-29|via=[[University of California, San Diego]]|website=Department of Mathematics}}</ref> advised by [[Peter Wai-Kwong Li]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lei Ni|url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=40047|access-date=2025-11-29|publisher=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]}}</ref> Ni was an assistant professor at [[Purdue University]] from 1998 to 2000 and at [[Stanford University]] from 2000 to 2002, before moving to UC San Diego in 2002.<ref name="home"/>

From 2002 to 2005, Ni worked as an assistant professor at UCSD, and from 2005 to 2009 as an associate professor.<ref name="home"/> He received a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fellows Database|url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database|access-date=2025-11-29|language=en|publisher=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]]}}</ref> Ni served as chair of the mathematics department from 2016 to 2020,<ref name="home"/> during which time, in 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|title=UC San Diego Mathematics Multiplies Excellence by Three|url=https://today.ucsd.edu/story/UC_San_Diego_Mathematics_Multiplies_Excellence_by_Three|website=UC San Diego Today|access-date=2025-11-29|language=en|date=November 17, 2017|last=Dillon|first=Cynthia|publisher=[[UC San Diego]]}}</ref> he was elected a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] for "contributions to [[geometric analysis]], particularly to [[Ricci flow]], and for mentorship".<ref>{{Cite web|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/grants-awards/fellows-list|access-date=2025-11-29|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]}}</ref> Since 2025, Ni has been an emeritus professor with Distinguished Professor title,<ref name="home" /> in recognition of his career at the university.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Salary Programs and Scales|url=https://aps.ucsd.edu/compensation/apo-salary.html#off-scale-and-above-scale-salary|website=Academic Personnel Services|access-date=2025-11-29|publisher=[[UC San Diego]]}}</ref>

His research areas include geometric analysis, [[Riemannian geometry]], and [[partial differential equation]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lei Ni|url=https://math.ucsd.edu/people/profiles/lei-ni|website=Department of Mathematics|access-date=2025-11-29|publisher=[[UC San Diego]]}}</ref> He has given talks on these topics to the [[Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Personal Profile: Lei Ni|url=https://www.slmath.org/people/3346?reDirectFrom=link|access-date=2025-11-29|publisher=[[Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute]]}}</ref> His publications on the Ricci flow include a 2006 book in the [[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]] series,<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hamilton’s Ricci Flow|last=Chow|first=Bennett|date=2006|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|isbn=978-1-4704-7369-3|last2=Lu|first2=Peng|last3=Ni|first3=Lei|series=Graduate Studies in Mathematics|volume=77|url=https://bookstore.ams.org/view?ProductCode=GSM/77}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hamilton's Ricci Flow|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/hamiltons-ricci-flow|access-date=2025-11-30|date=2007-05-18|last=Berg|first=Michael|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|website=MAA Reviews}}</ref> and a four-part book in [[Mathematical Surveys and Monographs]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Chow |first=Bennett |title=The Ricci Flow: Techniques and Applications |last2=Chu |first2=Sun-Chin |last3=Glickenstein |first3=David |last4=Guenther |first4=Christine |author-link4=Christine Guenther |last5=Isenberg |first5=James |author-link5=James Isenberg |last6=Ivey |first6=Tom |last7=Knopf |first7=Dan |last8=Lu |first8=Peng |last9=Luo |first9=Feng |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |author-last10=Ni |author-first10=Lei|postscript=:}}
*{{Cite book |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/view?ProductCode=SURV/135 |title=Part I: Geometric Aspects |date=2007 |isbn=978-0-8218-3946-1 |series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs |volume=135}}
*{{Cite book |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/view?ProductCode=SURV/144 |title=Part II: Analytic Aspects |date=2008 |isbn=978-0-8218-4429-8 |series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs |volume=144}}
*{{Cite book |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/view?ProductCode=SURV/163 |title=Part III: Geometric-Analytic Aspects |date=2010 |isbn=978-0-8218-4661-2 |series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs |volume=163}}
*{{Cite book |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/view?ProductCode=SURV/206 |title=Part IV: Long-Time Solutions and Related Topics |date=2015 |isbn=978-0-8218-4991-0 |series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs |volume=206}}</ref><ref>See reviews:
*{{Cite journal|title=Book reviews: ''The Ricci ﬂow'' and ''Hamilton’s Ricci ﬂow''|journal=[[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]]|date=February 2008|pages=176–179|volume=40|issue=1|doi=10.1112/blms/bdm088|language=en|first=Paul|last=Baird}}
